card_title: When the Wait Makes Us Casual
description: Israel had a saying: time passes, and prophecies come to nothing. We do the same thing when the wait gets long.
excerpt: Just because something hasn't happened yet doesn't mean it isn't going to. God doesn't move by our calendar. His delays aren't denials.
verse: "Son of man, you've heard that proverb they quote in Israel: 'Time passes, and prophecies come to nothing.'"
body_html:
I'll admit, Ezekiel was never one of my favorite books to read. He comes across as eccentric and honestly a little out there in places. But the more I read him, the more a lot of what he said feels like it's written straight into our world today.

The people of Israel had a saying going around. Time passes, and prophecies come to nothing. God had been warning them for years through prophets, and so far, nothing bad had actually happened. So they started getting comfortable. They started mocking the warnings. The joke basically became, "yeah, yeah, the prophets keep saying stuff and nothing ever happens, so why take any of it seriously?"

We do the same thing.

The end times are near. Jesus is coming back on this date. Signs are everywhere. These prophecies will be fulfilled by this year. We've heard it so many times from so many voices that it can start to feel like none of it is real. Like we're all just believing a thing that never actually arrives. Like it's a story people tell themselves.

That slow drift into skepticism is dangerous. Because the same God who was working on His own timetable back in Ezekiel's day is the One in control of the timetable now.

Just because something hasn't happened yet doesn't mean it isn't going to. God doesn't move by our calendar. His delays aren't denials, and His silence isn't absence. And He warned us that the last days would include people mocking the very idea that Jesus is coming back. That mocking was predicted too.

The people in Ezekiel's day thought nothing was going to happen until the day it did. And when it did, it was everything they'd been warned about.

I don't want to be casual about what God has said. I don't want to assume His patience means He's not going to act. I'd rather live like He could come back today and be wrong about the timing than live like He never will and be wrong about the whole thing.

Have you let the length of the wait make you casual about what God has said is coming?
question: Have you let the length of the wait make you casual about what God has said is coming?
